items.followUp: State the commutative law of Boolean algebra.

rubric.why: Both associative identities are stated correctly.
rubric.description: Associative law for OR and AND
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each correct identity.

modelAnswer: Associative law for OR: (A + B) + C = A + (B + C).
Associative law for AND: (A · B) · C = A · (B · C).

items.followUp: What does a software licence allow a user to do?

rubric.why: Identifies copyright as legal protection or rights belonging to the creator or owner.
rubric.description: Protection of the creator or owner's work
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying legal protection or rights for the creator/owner.

rubric.why: States that copying or distributing copyrighted work without permission is prohibited.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that use, copying, or distribution requires permission.

modelAnswer: Copyright law gives the creator or owner legal protection and rights over their original work, including software.
It prevents others from copying, using, or distributing that work without permission.

rubric.why: Recognizes that one licensed copy is being used on more computers than the licence allows.
rubric.description: Using one licensed copy on multiple computers beyond the licence
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying use beyond the licence's permitted number of computers.

rubric.why: Identifies soft lifting as unauthorized software copying or use.
rubric.description: Unauthorized copying or use of software
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the action as unauthorized copying or use.

modelAnswer: Soft lifting is copying or installing a licensed software program on more computers than the licence permits.
It is unauthorized use of software and is a form of software piracy.

items.followUp: What is file sharing on a computer network?

rubric.why: States that an application is made available to multiple users over a network.
rubric.description: Sharing an application over a network
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that users share or access an application through a network.

rubric.why: Explains that users can use the shared application rather than each needing a separate local installation.
rubric.description: Users can use the shared application from their computers
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that multiple users can use the shared application from their computers.

modelAnswer: Application sharing allows users on a network to access and use the same application.
The application can be used from different computers without installing a separate copy on each one.

items.followUp: State two disadvantages of star topology.

rubric.why: Identifies that the failure of one attached device does not disrupt the other devices.
rubric.description: Failure of one device does not affect the others

rubric.why: Identifies an advantage such as easy expansion, removal, or fault detection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one of these advantages.

modelAnswer: Failure of one computer or device does not affect the other devices on the network.
It is easy to add or remove devices, and faults are easier to locate.

items.followUp: Define a switch in a computer network.

rubric.why: Identifies that a router connects different networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a router connects networks.

rubric.why: Explains that a router directs packets between networks, commonly using IP addresses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing packet forwarding or routing.

modelAnswer: A router is a networking device that connects different networks.
It forwards data packets between them toward their destination, using IP addresses.

items.followUp: What is the function of the Transport layer in TCP/IP?

rubric.why: Names the four TCP/IP layers. The first two named layers earn 1 mark; the remaining two earn 1 mark.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Application and Transport; award 1 mark for Internet and Network Access.

modelAnswer: The TCP/IP layers are Application, Transport, Internet, and Network Access.

items.followUp: Which HTML tags are used to create a definition list?

rubric.why: States that a definition list pairs terms with their definitions or descriptions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the content of a definition list.

rubric.why: Identifies the HTML tags used for the list, its terms, and their descriptions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming <dl>, <dt>, and <dd> or describing their roles.

modelAnswer: An HTML definition list presents terms together with their definitions or descriptions.
It uses <dl> for the list, <dt> for each term, and <dd> for its definition.
